title: UPC Barred from Fielding Presidential Candidate in 2026 Elections Amid Leadership Crisis
description:
The Uganda People's Congress (UPC), one of Uganda’s oldest and most influential political parties, has been disqualified from fielding a presidential candidate in the 2026 general elections. The Electoral Commission (EC) cited ongoing internal disputes, breaches of the party constitution, and binding court rulings as the primary reasons for the unprecedented decision.

At the center of the controversy is Jimmy James Michael Akena, the current party president. A High Court ruling in Miscellaneous Cause No. 148 of 2025 determined that Akena had already served the maximum two terms permitted under the UPC constitution. Despite attempts by the party to extend his tenure through a virtual extraordinary delegates’ conference, the EC declared these actions unconstitutional and invalid.

The disqualification also affected other senior UPC figures. Denis Enap Adim failed to meet the constitutional requirements for nomination, while Peter Walubiri Mukidi was excluded for not participating in the official nomination process. The situation has deepened a leadership crisis that has left the party fragmented and facing uncertainty ahead of the elections.

Social media platforms have been rife with speculation and false reports, including claims that Akena had been cleared to contest. These claims were swiftly refuted by legal representatives within the UPC, emphasizing that no nominations had been officially approved by the EC.

Founded in 1960, the UPC has a long and storied history in Uganda’s political landscape. The party played a leading role in the country’s transition to independence in 1962 under Milton Obote and the alliance with the Kabaka Yekka party. Over the decades, the UPC has experienced periods of both prominence and marginalization, but it has remained a symbol of Uganda’s post-independence political evolution.

Political analysts warn that the party’s absence from the 2026 presidential race could significantly reshape the electoral landscape. With opposition parties and new political movements gaining traction, UPC’s disqualification may alter voter alignments and influence coalition dynamics.

Party insiders admit that resolving the internal disputes and restoring cohesion will be a monumental challenge. With the nomination deadline approaching, UPC is confronted with the stark reality of potentially missing the presidential race for the first time in its history. Observers say this moment represents both a critical test for the party and a reflection of the broader challenges facing established political organizations in Uganda today.
author: Kyoga TV

title: Premier League Weekend Roundup: Drama at Old Trafford, Late Arsenal Rescue, and Villa’s Woes Continue
description:
Red cards, late drama and missed chances defined another gripping weekend in the Premier League.
From Manchester United’s chaotic victory over Chelsea to Arsenal’s stoppage-time equaliser against Manchester City, fans were treated to a round of football that underlined just how unpredictable the season is shaping up to be.

At Old Trafford, Manchester United breathed life into their stuttering campaign with a 2-1 victory over Chelsea. The match was turned on its head inside the first five minutes when Chelsea goalkeeper Robert Sánchez was sent off for a reckless foul. United seized the advantage, with Bruno Fernandes marking his 100th goal for the club before Casemiro doubled the lead. The Brazilian midfielder’s afternoon ended early too, dismissed before half-time to even the numbers. Chelsea’s Trevoh Chalobah struck late to set up a nervy finish, but Erik ten Hag’s side held firm to secure three vital points.

The weekend’s showpiece clash at the Emirates did not disappoint. Manchester City looked on course for victory after Erling Haaland’s early strike, but Arsenal grew into the contest, pressing relentlessly in search of an equaliser. Their persistence was rewarded deep into stoppage time, when Gabriel Martinelli latched onto a clever pass from Eberechi Eze to rescue a 1-1 draw. The result keeps both sides firmly in the title conversation, though City may rue letting two points slip so late.

Aston Villa’s wait for a first league win of the season continued, despite facing ten-man Sunderland at the Stadium of Light. Matty Cash gave Unai Emery’s side a rare lead, only for Wilson Isidor to equalise after Sunderland’s Reinildo had been shown red. Emery did not mince words afterwards, branding his side’s performance “lazy” as pressure mounts on Villa to turn their season around.

Nottingham Forest’s Ange Postecoglou remains without a Premier League win, though he insists progress is being made. Forest took the lead through Neco Williams against Burnley but were pegged back as the match finished 1-1. It is the third straight game without victory for Forest under the Australian coach, whose attacking philosophy has yet to translate into results.

Across the league, fine margins defined the weekend’s drama: United clinging on with ten men, Arsenal’s stoppage-time lifeline, Villa’s inability to punish a weakened Sunderland, and Forest’s missed chances for a breakthrough win. With the table beginning to take shape, every point feels crucial, and this weekend showed again why the Premier League remains the most unpredictable competition in world football.

Weekend Results at a Glance
- Manchester United 2–1 Chelsea
- Arsenal 1–1 Manchester City
- Sunderland 1–1 Aston Villa
- Nottingham Forest 1–1 Burnley
author: Olica Felix

title: Rebecca Kadaga Returns to Busoga: A Homecoming of Loyalty, Unity, and Cultural Pride
description:
In a remarkable display of political resilience and regional solidarity, former Speaker of Parliament and First Deputy Prime Minister Rebecca Alitwala Kadaga was welcomed back to her home region of Busoga in a series of jubilant celebrations. This marked her first public appearance in the region following her defeat in the National Resistance Movement (NRM) Central Executive Committee (CEC) elections on August 27, 2025.

Thousands of supporters from across Busoga thronged the streets of Jinja and Kamuli, creating a colorful procession that spanned kilometers. The celebration began at Busoga Square in Jinja and moved towards the National Agricultural Showgrounds, while a parallel event unfolded at Kamuli Municipal Council playground. The massive turnout underscored Kadaga’s enduring influence and popularity in the region, cutting across political lines.

In her address, Kadaga reaffirmed her commitment to the NRM, emphatically declaring, 'I am still a fully subscribed member of the NRM party, and no one will push me out.' Her statement comes amid speculation about her political future following the recent CEC elections and signals her determination to remain an influential figure within the party.

The event was more than a political rally—it was a celebration of Busoga’s rich cultural heritage. Traditional dances and performances punctuated the day, highlighting the region’s customs and reinforcing the sense of communal pride. Leaders from various political parties, including the NRM, National Unity Platform (NUP), and Forum for Democratic Change (FDC), joined the celebrations, showcasing an unusual but significant display of political unity.

Kadaga also addressed tensions within the region, taking a subtle swipe at Busoga Premier Muvawala for alleged attempts to undermine her efforts. She called for collaboration and collective action to advance Busoga’s development, urging leaders and citizens alike to prioritize the region’s interests over political rivalry.

Observers noted that Kadaga’s homecoming was not only a reaffirmation of her political relevance but also a testament to her ability to unite diverse factions and maintain her standing as a key figure in Uganda’s political landscape. As the 2026 general elections approach, her continued influence in Busoga could play a pivotal role in shaping regional and national politics.

The day concluded with jubilant celebrations, leaving attendees energized and hopeful for a future in which political loyalty, unity, and cultural pride converge.

title: Elle Trivia Muhoza Crowned Miss Uganda 2025/26 at Glamorous Grand Finale
description:
Elle Trivia Muhoza, a 22-year-old from Bukomansimbi District, has been crowned Miss Uganda 2025/26 at a spectacular ceremony held on Saturday evening at the Sheraton Kampala Hotel. The event was streamed live on StarTimes Uganda’s Makula Kika channels, captivating audiences across the country with a celebration of beauty, intelligence, and ambition.

Muhoza succeeds Natasha Nyonyozi, the outgoing Miss Uganda 2024/25. The first runner-up was Faith Kirabo, while Agatha Drakes Keine was crowned second runner-up.

The evening featured a dazzling performance by renowned musician Grace Nakimera, adding to the glamour and excitement of the event. In addition, TikTok star Aminah Nalubega, popularly known as Errands Runner, captured the hearts of viewers, winning the Miss Popularity crown through overwhelming online support.

Organizers highlighted Muhoza Trivia’s victory as a celebration of 'beauty with a purpose,' emphasizing her goal to inspire young Ugandan women while pursuing her dreams in aviation.

Kyoga TV congratulates Elle Trivia Muhoza and wishes her success as she represents Uganda on the international stage.

title: Seven NUP Candidates Cleared in Lango, Signaling New Political Contest
description:
The National Unity Platform (NUP) has this week cleared seven candidates from the Lango sub-region to contest in the 2026 parliamentary elections, marking a significant expansion of the party’s presence in northern Uganda.

The approved candidates include:
- David Galla Okullo (Oyam North)
- Omang Emmanuel (Kole South)
- Edam Edward (Kole North)
- Ageno Harriet (Woman MP, Dokolo District)
- Enyum Denise (Kioga County, Amolatar)
- Enyang Churchill (Northern Region MP for Persons with Disabilities)
- Otim Maxwell (Otuke County)

The vetting process, which started on September 15, 2025, at the party headquarters in Makerere-Kavule, aimed to ensure transparency, discipline, and issue-based campaigns ahead of next year’s general elections.

Analysts note that NUP’s decision to field candidates across multiple districts in Lango could significantly alter the political landscape in a region historically dominated by the ruling National Resistance Movement (NRM) and the Uganda People’s Congress (UPC).

“This is a strategic move to broaden our presence and offer voters a strong alternative in the upcoming elections,” a party official said.

With the 2026 elections approaching, political watchers in Lango are keenly observing how these new entrants will influence voter dynamics and campaign strategies.

For continuous updates on this story and other political developments in Uganda, visit [Kyoga TV News](https://www.kyogatv.com/news).

title: Museveni Urges Lango to Form Committee to Resolve Stalled Cattle Compensation
description: President Museveni has called on the people of Lango sub-region to select a trusted committee to engage the government on the long-stalled cattle compensation program. Residents demand transparency, prioritization of verified claims, and elimination of middlemen. The committee’s formation is seen as a potential solution to restore trust and expedite payments.
author: Olica Felix

title: Seven Dead After Boat Capsizes on Lake Kyoga in Northern Uganda
description: A tragic accident occurred on Lake Kyoga in Amolatar District on September 19, 2025, when a boat carrying 36 passengers capsized, resulting in seven fatalities and 29 survivors. The victims have been identified as Steven Odeke (65) from Muchora Abino A village, Catherine Aguti (55) from Okwalongen Sub-county, Dokolo District, Sylvia Abonyo (35) from Amuda village, Soroti District, Jaspher Ogwal (38) from Corner Bileo Trading Centre, Arwotcek Sub-county, Robina Ejang (30) from Alemere Bung Cell, Epel Ward, Semmy Agwech (20) from Etam Sub-county, and Aboyi Nama (male adult, area not specified). The boat struck a tree stump near Kiryanga Village, and authorities are investigating the incident while urging residents to adhere to safety regulations on the lake.
